original.Title / subject: Minimal Change Disease vs. FSGS Selectivity
original.Statement / description: Minimal Change Disease presents with selective proteinuria (predominantly albumin due to charge barrier loss), whereas FSGS causes non-selective proteinuria with larger proteins lost due to structural podocyte loss.

original.Title / subject: Bartter Syndrome vs. Gitelman Syndrome Transporter Targets
original.Statement / description: Bartter syndrome phenocopies loop diuretics by affecting the NKCC2 transporter in the TAL (causing hypercalciuria), while Gitelman syndrome phenocopies thiazide diuretics by affecting the NCC transporter in the DCT (causing hypocalciuria).
